battleMedic.flavor: Battle Medic — {target} spends a d{faces} Hit Die
battleMedic.needTarget: Battle Medic: target the one creature you are tending first.
battleMedic.noHitDice: Battle Medic: {name} has no Hit Dice left to spend.
battleMedic.noGM: Battle Medic needs the GM online to heal a creature you don't control.
battleMedic.failed: Battle Medic was rolled, but {name}'s Hit Die and HP couldn't be updated — tell the GM.
battleMedic.done: {name} spends a d{faces} Hit Die and regains {healed} HP. Hit Dice left: {value}/{max}.
battleMedic.doneShort: {name} spends a d{faces} Hit Die and regains {healed} HP.

enabled.name: Feature riders
enabled.hint: Elemental Adept, Elemental Affinity, Potent Spellcasting, Healer and Battle Medic are applied automatically. Turn off to go back to doing them by hand.

hdControls.name: Hit Dice − / + on character sheets
hdControls.hint: Shows a − and a + beside Hit Dice on the character sheet outside edit mode, to spend or regain one Hit Die.

rituals.name: Ritual Adept rituals
rituals.hint: For a wizard with Ritual Adept: unprepared ritual spells get a 'Rituals' group on the Combat HUD's Cast Spell panel, and casting one starts with 'Consume Spell Slot' unticked (tick it to spend a slot anyway). Turn off to go back to Argon's prepared-only list and dnd5e's default.

concentrationSummons.name: Concentration summons leave with concentration
concentrationSummons.hint: When a caster's concentration ends (dropped, broken, or a new concentration spell), the tokens that spell summoned (Flaming Sphere, Summon Dragon...) are removed from the map by the GM's client. Summons without concentration are never touched. Turn off to clean them up by hand.

longCasts.name: Longer casts on the Combat HUD
longCasts.hint: Spells with a casting time of a minute or more (Animate Dead, Create Undead) are on none of the Combat HUD's bars. This adds a 'Longer casts' group to the Action bar's Cast Spell panel, for any character. Turn off to reach them from the sheet only.

concentrationAutoBreak.name: A failed concentration save ends concentration
concentrationAutoBreak.hint: When a concentration save fails, the concentration ends at once (and its summons with it), as the card's Break Concentration button would. Kept as a button when the creature could still turn the failure around (Legendary Resistance, Indomitable, a Mind Sharpener, Bardic Inspiration). The save card also shows the DC and whether it failed.

castDefaults.name: Summons start with Place Summons ticked
castDefaults.hint: A summon spell's dialog opens with 'Place Summons' ticked and its creature choice showing (Summon Undead and Animate Dead ship with it off); untick it to cast without placing. A self-only spell's card (Shield) also leaves out creatures you had targeted earlier.

arcaneRecovery.name: Arcane Recovery picks its slots
arcaneRecovery.hint: After a wizard uses Arcane Recovery, a small window lists their spent slots of level 1 to 5, opening on the highest ones that fit the PHB budget (half the Wizard level, rounded up). Recover restores them. Turn off to restore slots on the sheet by hand.

projectiles.name: One button per ray or dart
projectiles.hint: Scorching Ray and Magic Missile make several rolls, each at a creature of the caster's choice. Their chat card gets one button per ray or dart (3, plus one for each slot level above the spell's, or each extra wand charge). Target a creature, then click the next button. Turn off to roll from the card's own button only.

summon.place: Click the map to place {name}. Right-click or Escape cancels.

arcaneRecovery.title: Arcane Recovery
arcaneRecovery.intro: Choose spent spell slots to recover: up to {cap} levels combined, none of level 6 or higher.
arcaneRecovery.done: {name} recovers spell slots by studying the spellbook: {slots}.
arcaneRecovery.none: Arcane Recovery: no spent slots of level 1 to 5 to recover.
arcaneRecovery.changed: Arcane Recovery: the spell slots changed while the window was open, so nothing was recovered.

ray.status: Scorching Ray at level {level}: {done} of {count} rays rolled. Target one creature, then click the next ray.
ray.oneTarget: Each ray strikes one creature: target just one, then click the ray.

dart.status: Magic Missile at level {level}: {done} of {count} darts rolled. Target one creature, then click the next dart.
dart.oneTarget: Each dart strikes one creature: target just one, then click the dart.

projectiles.noTarget: No creature targeted: the roll goes ahead untargeted.
